sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
The core gameplay mechanics of Tiny Cars are simple yet engaging. The game is a top-down racing game, where you compete against six rivals on 15 diverse circuits. The game is easy to learn, but difficult to master, making it perfect for players who want to compete against others without feeling overwhelmed.

The gameplay is divided into several key components, including the car's acceleration, braking, and handling. The car's acceleration is crucial, as it allows you to quickly get up to speed and overtake your opponents. The braking system is also important, as it helps you to maintain control of your car and avoid accidents. The handling system is crucial, as it affects how your car responds to the track and obstacles.

The game also features several key power-ups and items that can be collected during gameplay. These include electric weapons, nitro speed bursts, and teleportation devices. Electric weapons allow you to damage your opponents and give yourself an advantage on the track. Nitro speed bursts give you a temporary speed boost, allowing you to overtake your opponents and get ahead on the track. Teleportation devices allow you to instantly move to a different location on the track, giving you a strategic advantage over your opponents.

Overall, the core gameplay mechanics of Tiny Cars are engaging and challenging, making it a great game for players who want to experience the thrill of racing without feeling overwhelmed.
